notes.title: Adding more depth and fun to edicts!
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

The latest Revival playtest is over, and our team is busy processing data and feedback from players. While that is being done, we want to share the changes that have taken place in the edicts system, as well as the latest visual effects work.  

Long-time players know that the [b]Temperature Decrease[/b] edict, as the name implies, lowers the temperature in affected hexes. A desert climate turns into a tropical one, a tropical climate morphs into a temperate climate… you get the picture. Here's what the updated visuals of this edict look like.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/85881732a765379fb7a197c07c4c88c2945e39b5.gif[/img]

If [b]Temperature Decrease[/b] is now applied to a hex with a unit standing on it, they will be surrounded by blocks of ice coming out of the ground.  

That’s right! Each strategic edict available on the global map can now also be used in battle. The effects of these micro edicts only last during combat. Unlike global edicts, a micro edict works immediately, and one cannot interfere with it by destroying the capsule the edict was launched from. But you have the ability to launch a counter-edict, which can cancel or alter the effect of the enemy's. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/c24650fd057ba253131ea9f26f8d310d9d44ffd9.png[/img]

The image above shows the effects of some edicts on the game map. Here are just a few of them:

[list]
[*] If you launch the [b]Acid Rain[/b] edict in a Cold climate, an acidic glacier will form in its place. 

[*] The [b]Spore Germination[/b] edict creates a shrub on the target hex and the six closest hexes. It will spawn vines and roots that entangle an enemy unit, preventing them from moving for two turns. 

[*] A [b]Contamination[/b] edict will appear as a crack in the ground with a radioactive glow. Until the rift is closed, zombies will emerge from it, attacking all factions indiscriminately, except for other zombies and automatons. 
[/list]
Speaking of cracks, below are the updated visuals for the Earthquake edict.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/f7f8da647f77f9d3d92055e1db5df24e9338d9cb.gif[/img]

More cool changes are coming in the near future! We hope to release an updated game build in about 4 weeks time. Look forward to your comments and feedback ;) 

Yours faithfully, 
Revival: Recolonization Team

The ballista is an assault weapon used to break through the enemy's front line. Simple versions of the ballista do not require strategic resources to create, but they will do less damage. Copper ballistas do moderate damage, while bronze ones deal high damage and have higher penetration ability. Of course, making them out of iron or titanium will greatly increase their effectiveness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/7d71629af40d3b2b1be615886b0dad46ed7281cb.png[/img]

Yours faithfully, 
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Getting ready for war

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/83db8ec59aad0a14406e8aed7e9f0a92dff16d65.png[/img]

Work on the edict system continues in the current development cycle. notes.title: Upcoming Tribe Update
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Tribes have always been an important part of the Revival: Recolonization. In the upcoming update, our team wanted to expand on the idea of tribes and introduce more depth and replayability to this game system. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/3225ab2420f50a5134ee155e996e5b8801a615c2.jpg[/img]

As you may already know, there are currently 5 tribes in Revival. Each tribe has a predisposition to a certain climate type: Cold, Cool, Temperate, Hot and Desert. 

[list]
[*]Cultists of Eternal Ice. These wild savages and fearless warriors worship the Heavenly Liberator, bringing madness wherever they go. 
[*]Heresy Hunters. Fanatical warriors, defenders of subarctic lands from servants of the All-Mind and the barbarians from the icy wasteland.
[*]Children of the Vault. Descendants of the once civilized townspeople that survived the cataclysm in an underground bunker. They are not particularly strong in military affairs, but are always happy to rebuild civilization anew.
[*]Heavenly Fire Custodians. In the collective memories of these people, the cataclysm that struck Earth has etched itself in the form of a cleansing fire from the skies. Each tribesman views death by fire as an honour. 
[*]Ash Commissaries. Magistrates from the hot desert, protectors of trade caravans.
[/list]
Every tribe consists of a number of clans - separate settlements on the game map, each with their own chieftain. Each clan has three clan traits that determine its social composition and cultural values. When you pick a clan to lead, your faction inherits all three of its traits, as well as a unique trait of the tribe your chosen clan belongs to.

Your choice of clan at the beginning of the game influences how the game session will play out. To lead a bunch of desperate savages and cutthroats, or a peace-loving group of scientists and farmers – it is up to you to decide!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/6e1a645157cde0ab21a27dac1eaba4333adde8d3.png[/img]

By assimilating clan after clan, your faction will be able to gain new traits, becoming more and more unique in the process. 

Clan traits are distributed randomly when the game world is generated. However, there are a few limitations related to a clan’s tribe alignment.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/344486fb6e5fa7aaa2c7dab280bea20bf9561514.jpg[/img]

For example, clans belonging to the Children of the Vault tribe cannot have the “savages'' trait, since members of this tribe tend to be more technologically savvy than others. Ash Commissaries clans cannot have the "murderer" or "thief" traits, since they go against the tribe’s cultural and philosophical views. 

The Tribe Update will be launching in the next 1-2 weeks, depending on how QA goes. Get ready to immerse yourself in the intricacies of tribes and clans coming to Revival!

Yours faithfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Machine vs Man: Meet the All-Mind
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

In previous updates, we have gone over some of the mechanics of Revival: Recolonization and how the game is changing based on your feedback. What we haven't discussed in as much detail is the game’s premise. Today, we are going to talk about the creation of the All-Mind and the fall of humanity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/8a86884901bce54d67f41fc905f2ed313befbbb4.png[/img]

Thousands of years ago, humankind reached its technological zenith. Man was able to explore the galaxy and travel to new planets, terraforming them into habitable homes.

This new era of development marked the creation of an artificial intelligence called the All-Mind. Though its intelligence surpassed that of its architects, the international team of scientists working on the project pushed their new creation even further. By tethering together the lithospheric plates of many planets via portals, they created something that resembled the neural network of a human brain. As a result, a breakthrough was made - the All-Mind's intelligence and power grew to a point where it seemed almost supernatural.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/6a85b970387f748bf5611ab7d3e49e459ab4125e.jpg[/img]

The All-Mind looked down upon its creators and saw humanity as weak, feeble – it fancied itself as the next stage in human evolution. Without the slightest hesitation, the rogue A.I would destroy life on any given planet, guided by curiosity and inexplicable spite. The team of scientists responsible for the All-Mind project realized their mistake too late. A few of them tried to destroy the neural network by disconnecting the portals at the cost of their own lives.

This resulted in the All-Mind losing its sanity and launching a galaxy-wide cataclysm full of destruction and chaos. The incident severely altered the climates and orbits of various settled planets, forever changing them and plunging humanity into a new Dark Age.

Each of these planets still holds fragments of the All-Mind, disconnected from the neural network and hibernating for a thousand years. This is when you wake up from cryosleep - a member of the team of scientists that created the tyrannical A.I. It will be up to you to correct the mistakes of the past or to succumb to them and unleash the All-Mind’s madness yet again. The choice is yours and yours only.

Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Killing in the name of peace
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Last time, we looked at how diplomacy works in Revival: Recolonization. Today, we're talking about tribes, their worldviews, and how your actions affect them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/c322b227327fc6781898800ea02a2143774f334b.jpg[/img]

Over the hundreds of years since the great cataclysm, humanity has split into several factions as people tried to survive the end of the world. Each group worships or despises a wide range of ideologies and traditions. You'll find some of these ideas to be relatable, while others may be completely alien. Either way, you cannot just ignore them; each tribe is fiercely devoted to their long-held traditions.

Each tribe's way of life influences their trade, expansion and actions towards you. Actions that one group might like could be unpopular with another. For example, when you build military units, tribes with a militaristic worldview will approve of this action, but the pacifists won't. Tribes with similar philosophies will get along better than those with different worldviews. That sounds simple enough, right? Well, we're not done yet.


Every single thing you do will influence how tribes see you. Growing totem trees, cutting down forests, issuing edicts, destroying automatons or even manipulating communications can have drastic effects on different groups.

Don't worry, you don't have to please everyone in Revival: Recolonization! No matter what you do, you'll always find allies with a similar approach to survival.

Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Free tribes and vassals
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

In our previous communiqué, we talked about the basics of diplomacy in Revival, as well as how reputation and loyalty tie into the system. While the main political powers in the game are factions led by emissaries, one should not discount regular human tribes that have been surviving alongside a mad A.I. ‘God’ for centuries. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/2c6660a86382596b346d16b5734b70a551c0b495.jpg[/img]


To build your first city in Revival, you'll need to find a suitable tribe on the game map and take charge of it. Each tribe carries their own attitude towards other tribes, factions and emissaries, and also values slightly different things (from killing automatons to caring about Totem Trees). Thus, assimilating a tribe could worsen or strengthen your relations with other factions during a game session. 

In the future, tribes will also tie into the game’s event system, and we hope to add more game mechanics related to tribe management such as mythologies. But for now, let’s focus on what you’ll experience this June ;) 

When you discover a free tribe on the game map, you can:
[list]
[*]leave them alone
[*]make the tribe chief your vassal
[*]assimilate them (the tribe disappears from the map and joins the player's city)
[*]wipe them out
[/list]
Vassalization is usually the optimal way to coexist, though that can change depending on your playstyle. Tribes that are close to your lands can offer a variety of benefits if you can convince them to become your vassals: 
[list]
[*]trade discounts
[*]reduced cost of purchasing units
[*]unique resources from the area
[*]improved relations with other tribes and factions that hold the vassal in high regard
[*]etc.
[/list]
The better your relations with a tribe, the better the bonuses that your faction receives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/022a1adc4f88b8d71cf4f44cfbc2f1a0a9fc9e00.jpg[/img]

It is also beneficial to pay attention to inter-tribal relations. Adding two feuding tribes to your empire will negatively impact your relationship with both of them. A tribe may rebel if they dislike actions undertaken by you or the fact that you are giving their foes too much attention. They can even defect to another faction!

But don't worry – you can also attract rebellious tribes from other factions if their mindset seems closer to yours or if they have access to a particular resource that you seek. You can also assimilate troublesome tribes by simply annexing the region they're in. But you may lose a potential ally or a buffer between you and warring free tribes this way, so there’s pros and cons to consider. 

That is all for today! We'll talk about tribe mindsets and their effect on gameplay in future posts.

Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Backstabbing & Alliances: The Basics of Diplomacy
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

These past few months, we were busy with diplomacy mechanics. Diplomacy in Revival: Recolonization works on multiple, simultaneous levels – just like in real life! Today, we're going to talk about the fundamentals of this game system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/061c3e2eba358fff4d7bc0cd04eed80bc2eeac6b.png[/img]

Diplomacy is found in most 4x strategy games. For good reason - by engaging with it, players should feel their influence over the game world, as well as perceive reactions from other agents on the map. In Revival, there are two groups you can negotiate with: free tribes and factions.

Free tribes have no allegiances to anyone, but they can become vassals. On the other hand, factions are led by AI-controlled emissaries. They build their own empires, capture territories, claim resources, and pursue their own goals.

Whether you make allies or enemies with these groups depends on your emissary's philosophy, your tribe and your playstyle. Diplomatic relations are governed by "loyalty", a modifier that players can influence. In addition to loyalty, each player has a reputation score.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/3978c7c4bd5981bb761e43414487746e6c3eb725.jpg[/img]

Reputation is a resource – you can gain or lose reputation points. If one party wants to make a move against another, it will cost them reputation. The cost of these actions will depend on the opposing faction's loyalty and the duration of the action.

Players will accumulate reputation every turn. The rate of growth will depend on your relations with free tribes and factions, upgrades available from the science tree, along with your choice of emissary.

Loyalty is a scale and not a resource; it represents your relations with a specific neighbor. Loyalty can be affected by certain interactions between groups, such as cooperation, neutrality, hostility and war. But it is not a factor that severely prevents you, the player, from playing Revival the way you like.

For example, two factions with high loyalty can still fight each other. However, the higher the loyalty, the lower the reputation cost to make peace again. As an additional benefit - other peaceful actions will also cost less. 

It's certainly easier to start wars if your loyalty is low, but trade and scientific agreements will cost a lot more for their duration. However, much like in real life, you can manipulate loyalty by spreading rumors and giving gifts. So there’s benefits and drawbacks to consider, just like with most systems in 4x games. 

The team is working hard to make the Open Alpha available to you this June, and we're looking forward to hearing your feedback on diplomacy!

notes.title: Open Alpha and beyond
notes.content:
Hello to all the Revival fans out there! Work on the Open Alpha build is full steam ahead. Come this June, we will be inviting players, members of press and influencers to try out the latest version. The updated game will feature improved combat, revamped UI, a diplomacy system and an array of smaller refinements to the core game. But not everything went according to plan, as is often the case in game development :) 

This is the game’s producer, Vasiliy Tedeev. Let’s talk about upcoming changes and expectations for Revival in the near future. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/056b5571bfaaf48cd9511b7d80df55b01c58781b.png[/img]

[b] Diplomacy v1.0 added [/b]

Once you start exploring outside of your home region in Revival, you will soon encounter tribe settlements and representatives of other factions. Unlike the Closed Alpha build, where diplomatic interactions were almost non-existent, you will now be able to establish more complex relationships with these entities and turn some of them into your allies or vassals. 

We wanted players to use the various tribes under their control as bargaining chips on the diplomatic table. To achieve this, we’ve added a slew of options for manipulating tribe loyalty - trading, sending gifts, spreading rumours, etc.

We’ll go into more detail about this system in future dev diaries, so instead, I want to briefly talk about the reasoning behind implementing diplomacy at this stage of Revival’s development.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/b24a031c161000756c845406e2f831aea8cddf78.png[/img]

The short answer is - repercussions for your actions. If you can run around a game map and conquer every single settlement with no reaction from the game world and its inhabitants, then you aren’t really playing a 4x game, are you? Rather, the experience resembles a wargame or a turn-based combat game whose developers randomly decided to have a global map.

In my opinion, that is the real benefit of having even a fairly standard diplomacy system in a 4x game - it provides feedback to the player and makes the game world feel more alive. 

[b] Revamped UI [/b]

The Closed Alpha build featured a UI that was temporary at best, and a lot of players noticed that. This time, we had a chance to put more thought into the user experience. You can see a mockup of the new UI below.

While the reworked interface is more informative and easier to use, we are still not completely happy with it. With your help, our team aims to keep improving this aspect of the game over the course of the Open Alpha.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/15e2b905b077b8f998b90ded3983b6e43b9a609d.png[/img]

[b] What the future holds [/b]

Here’s what our original plans for the launch of Open Alpha looked like:

[strike]Combat improvements [/strike]
Edicts 2.0
[strike]Diplomacy system [/strike]
Tribe assimilation update
[strike]UX/UI improvements [/strike]

You’ll notice that not all of the items are crossed off, and deciding what systems to focus on until the Open Alpha launches was tough. Unintuitive UI and tutorial were at the top of the list of complaints from players, with the data matching the feedback we’ve received from you. Thus, priorities were re-adjusted to favor fixing these issues before we start introducing more changes to game systems and adding content. 

Most players saw potential in the edict system and the depth afforded by its presence in the game. But we are not there just yet, so our team will be busy refining edicts and making sure they present an interesting toolset for you to play around with in the coming months. The same can be said about tribe management and associated game mechanics. Not to mention new units, improvements to terrain, animations and sounds - there’s more cool stuff coming to Revival ;)

After the Open Alpha launches, we will continue updating the game build at least once a month. Future versions will be made available via the Steam Playtest functionality, so watch out for a news alert with instructions on how to participate. 

Finally, I wanted to say thank you for joining us on this journey. Keep playing, keep creating, enjoy life and stay safe!

notes.title: A powerful and mighty instrument - the music of Revival
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

While the dev team is busy updating Revival’s game mechanics, all for the purpose of bringing you a great strategy experience, let us talk about one of the most important aspects of a game's atmosphere - its soundtrack.

Music has a huge influence on how you experience a game. When you're immersed in gameplay, you might not even notice it - but your brain certainly does. The right piece of music can help immersion and heighten your experience, making it richer and more vivid.

[previewyoutube=fYyFlpZRaWM;full][/previewyoutube]

Revival’s title theme (which you can listen to via the link above) mixes a classical orchestral style with modern ambient sounds. This combination was no accident. Light electronic beats evoke complex futuristic computers and the emptiness of space, only to give way to an expressive orchestral theme that fills the empty space with volume and power. As soon as you see and hear Revival’s main menu, you already know that the task presented by the game is an important one: a quest to reclaim Earth, by all means necessary. 

We’ve decided that every emissary, epoch and tribe should have its own musical theme. From founding a city to developing your empire, the music will change in form and complexity to reflect the events that occur under your leadership. The game’s soundtrack will also take you and your people on a musical journey through four distinct time periods, from traditional folk sounds to more modern melodies.

Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Invisible Elephants and Acid Rounds
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

We have previously outlined some of the changes to combat mechanics in Revival: Recolonization. The enemy AI has been upgraded and the gameplay has evolved into a more "chess-like" system with more depth and variety added to the mix. So, what else do we have in store for you? Let's find out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/42ce36f57e7a39c684146e43ee1078c13ac39ad4.jpg[/img]

Revival’s unit editor contains three main components that allow you customize your units: body, weapon and gear, with the latter subdivided into ammo and support items. Thanks to a design overhaul by Alex Yegorenkov, who is handling combat, your choice of items can drastically affect the capabilities of your squad.

A ranged squad may be modified from an attack unit into a support one that is capable of barrage fire. All you need to do is equip them with incendiary ammo instead of armor-piercing rounds. This flexibility is crucial in the new system, where cooperation and synergy between squads matter. 

A standard flamethrower tank can be replaced with an acid-firing one – pretty scary, right? This weapon type creates toxic puddles that damage the armor of whoever steps in them. They can also be used for direct assaults against armored adversaries, which is a great tactic when taking on defensive opponents!

Keep in mind that even archers from the first epoch can still pose a threat to more advanced units should you find enough materials to equip them with uranium-tipped arrows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/950aa5132340edb7c9235fbc8d3a156f94d801dd.jpg[/img]

Support items – such as amulets that protect against long-range attacks – are just as important and are equipped in place of shields. However, this will make units more vulnerable in melee combat, so there are trade-offs to consider.

For extra protection, some items increase radiation and fire resistance. And, of course, there are invisibility devices. These engineering marvels can make even elephants undetectable. It's never been a better time to make the enemy fear your squad of four-legged ninjas! 

And that's just a taste of the new items players can use in their conquest. Our goal is to diversify the combat system and allow players to create hundreds of strategic combinations on the battlefield.

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: When Camouflage Works Too Well
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

In the past, we have shown you various concept art for weapons, units, and structures, alongside their finished in-game models. Today, we want to briefly talk about how the models are created and why the final in-game model can sometimes look very different from its initial design.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/5291b29b4b565b5120810ad2228abdd149fa7a77.jpg[/img]

When it comes to the creation of 3D models in Revival: Recolonization, there are several stages:

[olist]
[*] A game designer lays out specifications for the unit or structure. This involves looking at the finer details for each model, how it should look, and why.
[*] Concept work. The art department comes up with a 2D sketch or 3D render to be approved by the art director, which is then passed on to a 3D artist.
[*] In-engine implementation. This lets us test how the model looks and behaves in-game.
[/olist]

At HeroCraft, a 3D artist's work not only involves creating 3D models and their textures, but also working on and improving the design itself. A 3D artist can access the project directly in the Unity engine, allowing them to check the design of a particular model on the game map, in real-time and on the fly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/d6583ebc9d56d4802ef73d69f166eab495ce3920.jpg[/img]

Like many other 4X games, Revival: Recolonization features a 3D map that players can zoom in and out on. While it is a handy feature for players, it can be a headache for 3D artists. There's a delicate balance between a model that is highly detailed when zoomed in and readability when zoomed out.

If key elements of the design are difficult to distinguish on the map, the 3D artist will tweak the model. Sometimes, an initial design may have lots of extra details that look great in a static image, but only add visual clutter when presented in-game.

It's not just a matter of aesthetics. In 4X games, one needs to be able to see the fighting ability of their units at a glance. Designs must be distinguishable so that different units are easy to tell apart.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/89ae5421a4138d817220109f790318c5f3e1159c.jpg[/img]

The design process can have amusing results, as 3D artist Yemelyan Kholuyev explains. During a team discussion, it was suggested that the third-epoch tank should be dark green like most modern military vehicles. The third epoch in Revival resembles our own present-day level of development, so it made sense to use a similar color scheme.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/b8f143a15932d924b625f63abaeb802446e8cb6c.jpg[/img]

In reality, this color scheme made the tanks much harder to see on the game map. So when the tank model was placed on a forest hex, it seamlessly blended into its surroundings (see image on the left). The camouflage certainly did its job, but players would have a much harder time seeing the model on the map. And now you know why third-epoch tanks in Revival: Recolonization are light green :)

Until next time!

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: Take the Higher Ground With Lightsabers
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Previously, we've only talked about weapons that already exist in our world or will do so in the foreseeable future. Today, we're talking about a very popular futuristic weapon that can exist only in theory, as any hardcore and heartbroken fan will tell you. Time to talk about the lightsaber.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/b6528a0d844a58483efa453636fbcf4ee1fc1fda.jpg[/img]

The lightsaber was first described in 1933 by Edmond Hamilton in the story Kaldar: World of Antares, and has since appeared in numerous works of fiction. Despite attempts by fans of various franchises, as well as military developments, there has yet to be a single working prototype of such a weapon.

You're already familiar with laser weapons and how they work: they fire a powerful beam over a huge distance, hitting everything in their path. This makes the lightsaber impossible in the real world – light cannot be "cut off" or have the specific, convenient length typical of swords (which also ensures the safety of whoever's using it). They also can't be solid, as depicted in Star Wars. And while the sword uses plasma rather than a laser, it is not possible to combine the two states of matter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/add536d82cabdc1d6c599631007b8dc0682fe64d.png[/img]

In Revival: Recolonization, the lightsaber is the only fourth-era melee weapon and is used for rear defense. Though equipped with advanced firearms, your fighters are still vulnerable if the enemy gets close to them. That is where lightsaber-wielding troops come in!

Lightsabers can also be used to break through enemy lines. Like laser guns, they ignore cover and ignite targets, enabling them to inflict significant damage even on well-defended units. The wound from the weapon itself may be minor, but a unit set on fire by a lightsaber can die within a few turns. Facing such enemies in battle requires a tactical approach—it's wise to avoid melee combat or be ready to put out burning soldiers. And no, elephant trunks can't be used as fire hoses, despite what the cartoons show you ;)

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: AI Combat Update: Man vs. Machine
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Our team is continuously working to improve and refine the combat system in Revival: Recolonization. A great deal has changed over the past few months, as we were busy implementing and testing new mechanics. Today, we are going to talk about one of the most important aspects of combat: enemy AI.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/6c962aa6538cd94aab6ea6f327b073befc4f7da3.jpg[/img]

In most turn-based strategy games, the AI is programmed to attack the player in a mostly straightforward manner using a basic set of skills. This tends to make the enemy's strategy predictable, leading to easy victories for the player. Creativity is what differentiates human players from AI — the inability to think outside of the box and make battles interesting.

To combat this issue, we decided on a chess-like system, where both the player and the AI use their limited number of units in the most constructive ways possible. Of course, they also need to take into account battlefield conditions, unit loadouts, and armor ratings. 

Players will no longer face treacherous full-frontal attacks from suicidal AI units. Instead, the AI will carefully choose when and where to attack the player. From the AI's first turn, it will assign a "weight" value to each hex and action, then follow through with an appropriate strategy. These values will be unique for each unit. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/66f451106e44a5f648a33b63b2459374eb0ad076.jpg[/img]

We've also ‘taught’ the combat AI to understand battle conditions. For example, enemy AI will know that units on fire can be extinguished by standing on a hex with water. You're probably thinking that you can use this to your advantage and lead the AI into a deadly ambush, but you'd be wrong. The AI managed to surprise even us by showing an ability to set its own traps. It's also learned to use environmental elements and combine them with rarely used skills. 

During testing, this unexpected behavior proved decisive to the AI's victory. Thus, we are also experimenting with different combat difficulties in order to allow players of any experience and skill level to enjoy this aspect of the game.

It's important to understand that the combat AI uses the same data that's available to players. There is no hidden information and both the player and the AI are on equal footing. When armies are matched in terms of strength and composition, human creativity and a cunning strategy can turn the tides of battle.

Be ready to test your mettle and combat chops in the Open Alpha!

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: The Plasmathrower: 8000 Degrees of Death
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

In our previous communiqué, we've talked about several types of futuristic weapons — each more amazing and devastating than the last. Today, we're going to talk about the Plasmathrower. 

While there isn't a working prototype available in the real world, development has been underway and making strides for almost fifty years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/97b62a0b2056e342a9e52a56418908669b9fc919.jpg[/img]

Plasma is the fourth state of matter. It is highly susceptible to magnetic fields and has a very high temperature. The operating principles of the plasmathrower are the same as those of other electromagnetic mass accelerators (gauss rifles and railguns), but it accelerates ionized gas instead of metal shots.

Plasma is characterized by a temperature of 8,000 degrees Celsius and is most often encountered in nature when you look at lightning strikes, or directly at the sun (don't do this without protection!). These impressive examples of nature demonstrate how difficult it is to construct and handle such weapons.

Currently, we use plasma cutters for cutting metals. These machines, which consume a lot of energy and are highly hazardous if mishandled, can cut through thick layers of sturdy material and are used in the construction of spacecraft.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/b0a9ad7fb6fefcad8a6e78aa48e31f786d920d06.jpg[/img]

As you may have already realized, the plasmathrower is the most powerful firearm in the game. It can easily burn through any cover; only very high-quality armor can stop its fiery stream. To defend against enemies wielding such powerful weapons, you must invest in the development and creation of exoskeletons, or use rare and unique resources to create body armor or cuirasses.

But even those may not be enough to save you. The reactor of the plasmathrower can be upgraded and enhanced if you have extra uranium or a few rare alternative resources obtained during your adventures. The enhanced plasmathrower is capable of incinerating enemy armor and whoever's wearing it, no matter what their defenses are. 

The inventions left by your forebears may help you create an unstoppable armor-piercing weapon. However, the soldiers wielding such weapons receive an impressive electric shock upon firing, which leaves them vulnerable for some time.

More info about the game's development coming soon. Stay put, associate ;)

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: Meet the EM Generator
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Our last message dealt with changes to the combat system and the importance of knowing how your enemy is equipped. Today, we're going to look at a unique fourth-age anti-vehicle weapon: the EM Generator.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/5d0f6cd47dba146e28b03414f3d17f3ec58a146e.jpg[/img]

In real life, electromagnetic weapons use either a magnetic field to propel a projectile — like a railgun — or electromagnetic radiation against a target.

[i]The EM generator in Revival: Recolonization[/i] features the latter and uses high-voltage currents to overload and disable electronics. While this is a non-lethal weapon designed to disable enemy vehicles, it also affects living creatures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/491cbc55912ea19181aa058483bc7546c6f5297b.jpg[/img]

All enemies within the damage radius will be hit by the EM current and suffer electrocution for two turns. Electrocuted units lose all of their action points, leaving them unable to attack or move. This leaves them vulnerable and easy targets for enemy forces.

By the second turn, the unit will start to recover and they'll be able to move and attack, but not hide. This situation may seem dire, but by the time you reach the fourth age, you'll already have encountered electric arrows and will know how to defend against and counteract them.

Remember: you can overcome any battle with the right equipment and mindset!

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: Laser Weapons
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Every year, more bleeding-edge technology is adapted for military use. Any innovation – even something so seemingly harmless as a laser – can be used on the battlefield. Today, we are going to talk about laser weapons and their role in [i]Revival: Recolonization[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/3cbcd3566e5c324a69143553e46f2727c4a015a9.jpg[/img]

Laser weapons focus light into a powerful beam that can cause utter devastation. The first laser was built in 1960, and since then the technology has been adopted by governments and corporations for military applications.

Experimentation with laser technology has led to the development of several variations, such as chemical and thermal. However, lasers are also widely used in the medical field.

So far, lasers aren't weaponised in modern-day warfare due to two major roadblocks:

[olist]
[*] Legislation: Any laser weapon designed to permanently blind targets are banned under Protocol IV of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons.

[*] Power: Using lasers on a large scale requires a massive amount of power, and battery technology has yet to advance far enough to make usage feasible.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/a9b4d2130aa7498cb1ce3d3a9b060ca5b35930db.jpg[/img]

But these constraints don't exist in the world of Revival: Recolonization. Technology in the game has advanced a step ahead of our own and combatants can use lasers to their full, destructive potential.

Unlike most other firearms, a laser's path of destruction is almost non-stop. The beams will pass through their target and continue in a straight line until they hit an immovable object, like a mountain. Standard lasers will deal a modest level of damage but set fire to everything they hit. A laser's battery can be supercharged to significantly increase its damage, but doing so causes the weapon to overload and electrocute whatever is wielding it, preventing them from moving.

When placing units on the battlefield, pay close attention to your enemy's arsenal and position your forces in strategic positions, away from danger. Remember, laser beams don't discriminate between friend and foe.

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team
[/b]

notes.title: How we are improving the combat system
notes.content:
[b]Greetings, loyal fans and associates![/b]

We would like to thank everyone for the invaluable feedback on Revival: Recolonization. You’ve given us an incredible amount of information to help improve the game before Open Alpha. As mentioned in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1306770/view/3035957285924272699]producer’s letter[/url], the last two months were spent retooling the game’s combat system. So what has changed, exactly?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/c1e12bb5cf5e6629b3fb2566fda9255675623d1c.jpg[/img]

The Closed Alpha game build featured a combat system that was fairly tactical, with a significant focus on climate, terrain type and other attributes. However, the battles ended up being drawn-out engagements in which raw military power played a decisive role in determining the victor. Not much point in tactics when you can simply squash enemies with a big enough army :)  

All of that has changed, hopefully for the better. Revival: Recolonization's new combat system is more akin to chess, with the movement and placement of units having a far greater impact on battles. More emphasis is placed on unique properties of the different weapons types, armor and equipment. Enemy units can be knocked back by shields, disoriented by protective equipment or paralyzed by electric arrows. Terrain type still plays a fundamental part in combat – hexes greatly influence the tide of battle by offering various kinds of protection and visibility bonuses to units.

To complement the new battle system, we also added new UI elements. Players will now see unit health and armor bars, a cover icon, movement points, and various status effects like radiation poisoning or fire. All of the information you need is now displayed in one easy-to-use and easy-to-read place. This should hopefully provide you with a superior overview of the battlefield.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/cab6d36d91eace4c67905acf03fc9593ac8594f4.jpg[/img]

And, finally, we have reworked the importance of various troop combinations. For example, a few tanks with advanced weaponry aren't necessarily powerful enough to defeat second-epoch soldiers that are well-equipped and strategically positioned on the battlefield. You won't be able to brute-force your way to victory in every battle.

Keep in mind that Revival: Recolonization features a unit editor that lets you experiment with different builds for your units. Bring your very own ideas to life, analyze your victories and defeats and learn how different tactics can complement each other. And remember: there's always a way out of a seemingly hopeless situation, you just need to figure it out.
[b]
Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: This is my rifle, this is my railgun
notes.content:
[b]Greetings, associate![/b]

In our previous communiqué, we talked about the various weapons of the first and second epochs in Revival: Recolonization. It is time to look to the future and discuss an advanced weapon that already exists in prototype form in the real world. Today, we're talking about railguns.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/e46419abd23f5d3259f81184a761afc3027ace08.jpg[/img]

A railgun is an electromagnetic mass accelerator that launches a conductive projectile along a pair of rails. It requires a high direct current to operate, which makes it cumbersome and unsuitable for individual use.

In Revival: Recolonization, the railgun is a weapon found in the fourth (and final) epoch. It is used by artillery troops as a replacement for catapults, cannons and missile launchers. 

The first real-world iteration of the railgun was invented in 1970 specifically to replace guided-missile systems. Pound for pound, railguns are 40,000 times more cost effective than missiles and can be used for both anti-air and anti-missile defense.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/b97d73f72beefeabd6011909c44454de75bb9fe1.jpg[/img]

While real-life railgun prototypes already exist, we're listing them as a futuristic weapon due to the present-day challenges in manufacturing them. This complex piece of technology requires an advanced level of military science and engineering, and we're unable to harness enough current to use them for military purposes just yet.

But (as you may have guessed from the concept above), anything is possible in Revival: Recolonization! Railguns are among the most powerful weapons in the game alongside plasma and singularity cannons, so playing around with them is fun. Just make sure your empire survives and reaches the final epoch ;)

[b]Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team[/b]

notes.title: Medieval rifles
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

In this entry about the more unusual weapons and equipment seen in Revival: Recolonization, we're going to take a look at a weapon that existed in our world much earlier than most people expect. It is time to talk about medieval guns of the second epoch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/677658edf0d3db5c6a2db8b031b2b2b8e8769ac5.jpg[/img]

Fantasy writers often neglect firearms in favor of swords and magic, creating a perception of the past that's far from the truth. Primitive firearms played a logical and essential role in medieval combat, as an increase in the use of heavy armor necessitated the creation of weapons more powerful than the bow and arrow.

In fact, the earliest forms of such firearms date back to 12th-century China – two hundred years before their appearance in Europe. While inaccurate and less effective at piercing armor than crossbows, they were valued for their ability to create smoke screens, deafening noise and a strong sulfur smell that scared horses.The metal balls used as ammo for this weapon were extremely expensive due to their lead content, so small rocks found on the battlefield often served as a suitable replacement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/3ade6759ec1d444ec516abc168c1b329c53d3132.jpg[/img]

During a playthrough of Revival: Recolonization, you will encounter a more advanced form of weaponry similar to an arquebus (a predecessor to the musket). The use and effectiveness of this initially crude weapon advanced rapidly in the 15th century, rivaling the bow and crossbow thanks to the fact that its projectiles weren't deflected by armor, didn't get stuck in shields and weren't affected by the wind.

But if you want to kit your armies out with firearms, you're going to need gunpowder. This was yet another crucial stage in the evolution of technology and firearms in our world – the invention of early gunpowder paved the way for more powerful forms of weaponry.
[b]
Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team
[/b]

notes.title: Medieval tanks
notes.content:
[b]Greetings, associate![/b]

In our last post, we spoke about war elephants – one of Revival: Recolonization's unusual mobile units. Today, we're going to look at the second epoch and the arrival of complex man-made mechanisms. More specifically, we're going to talk about tanks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/92027bcbc656bca8f8c58d42d77dcff44349bac0.jpg[/img]

The tanks most people are familiar with were first widely used during WWI, but early incarnations of the vehicle started appearing almost five hundred years earlier. Leonardo da Vinci is credited with designing one of the first tanks ever, drawing on concepts of mobile fortifications and siege towers dating back to antiquity. Enjoy a recreation of da Vinci’s design in the image above.

The idea never reached fruition and was forgotten, with simpler offensive weapons remaining in use for the next several centuries. Mobile fortifications of one kind or another appeared in various places around the world in the form of wagon forts, carroccios and other siege engines. They served as inspiration for our artists during the concept stage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/349e6dfb57d80c46f4976814cb6554d2e9acee51.jpg[/img]

But then we decided to go a step further - by the second epoch, humankind knows how to forge metal, so it only made sense to include blacksmithing crafts in the unit design of this epoch. 

That is why Revival: Recolonization has steam tanks! The reason they appear fairly early in the game is due to the inclusion of an external engine based on the combustion of any available raw material (just like the historical prototype that was created in our world). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/e2ed12b7b532650d2ffa01dea74ced02f4622a24.jpg[/img]


Tanks and other mobile units are designed to quickly break through enemy defense lines. The vehicle's treads allow it to navigate difficult terrain - if a tank enters a hex that contains a Forest, for example, the trees will be knocked down. A tank can even crush infantry units, but it is vulnerable against artillery fire, so rushing blindly into battle is never a good strategy. 

That is all for today!

Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: War Elephants of the New World
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!


It is time to tell you about one of Revival: Recolonization's most unusual units: the war elephant. Why were elephants chosen for battle? How do the elephants in Revival differ from their real-life counterparts? Read on to find out.

[img]https://ci5.googleusercontent.com/proxy/2k_SdaiuVjb0jJXFeVhbgyueA4DH0SloQbTTM6J43UXVaINKJkBSXpNG0S5jYHGmi8F5dScr02u7Z-lMDSKT5U-ngbMxj5TzbzVFOF-uayKmzHp4KdnQ7PKDKb6fbdk4HPKrOKlDYAWkkMleIrnV_fidax_uyut-LsbDEn8ywycq8k0EUQRMHd55z3FJ=s0-d-e1-ft#https://static.wixstatic.com/media/9d5e56_ff5e9b53684d4f589c21a89be00c766a~mv2.jpg/v1/fit/w_631,h_2000,al_c,q_85/image.jpg[/img]

Anyone who's seen war elephants in films will be familiar with the sight of wooden watchtowers and small fortifications for archers on the back of these giant creatures. In battle, elephants often carried up to four armed fighters and were used to suppress cavalry and intimidate the enemy. They were also irreplaceable when it came to traversing difficult terrain that was inaccessible to foot soldiers.


While the most famous battles where elephants were involved date back to antiquity and the middle ages, they continued to be in use in a few places around the world (mainly in Asia) up until the end of the 19th century. As one example, the Siamese army used war elephants outfitted with artillery up until the Franco-Siamese War of 1893. 

[img]https://ci6.googleusercontent.com/proxy/PBorhM4tyXyKhbF9W628Z7eWlnaBv2L-dLGeSdkQ0-eiDkd-na232PFZOU8IY0uAIBAAUhV8T6UtXIeB1jrhbTl1Mv4NVmcz2OI_FR0gyf2xArDTY_iXGkdtCGSIoAKvndX3yDUhSfSQtix9VWZJD46PvTR_Z1NY3-00VD3Tmc0jtU84PHhQvJko3sej=s0-d-e1-ft#https://static.wixstatic.com/media/9d5e56_a1fa1c18928a4859b0cd543ffac284d4~mv2.jpg/v1/fit/w_631,h_2000,al_c,q_85/image.jpg[/img]

While playing Revival: Recolonization, you may notice that elephants have undergone a few changes during the thousand years that have passed since the cataclysm. They have adapted to the changing environment by growing fur, so they look a lot more like the mammoths that came before them. The new breed of elephants is also bigger and stronger. With formidable tusks, huge legs and the ability to carry powerful armaments, they truly are magnificent creatures – terrifying and beautiful.

[img]https://ci4.googleusercontent.com/proxy/KJmfvDz65mETgz20RX2lCYvhJIXxXoweJtJqA4el0fCrxoI6MmYGF-Zc_0kp6HUyib7yfFYCLAaCvrBUFLlw4W8L2qs9MLz0wzNxAu_o-5e_E9nj1E0kkcbNIJJEzFiys7On2Ni3I-tj-vkVnAPA69iPmN1xSbx3daqUsKOtwx20Qub7xBVgdUIRz9Zj=s0-d-e1-ft#https://static.wixstatic.com/media/9d5e56_9dddd7465c6c43c893af55fa3ba5cfff~mv2.jpg/v1/fit/w_631,h_2000,al_c,q_85/image.jpg[/img]

In the first epoch, elephants can be equipped with heavy ballistas. From the second epoch and onwards, you can opt to replace the ballista on the back of an elephant with more powerful weapons, a gatling gun and even a laser cannon among them. Not bad for a species that has been around since the Pliocene epoch in our world, eh?


Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Weapons of War
notes.content:
Greetings, associate!

Today, we’d like to continue discussing combat in Revival and in particular – the thought process behind the unit editor.

Since the game’s inception, Vlad Mishukov, lead game designer, wanted to provide players with fun tools to play around with in terms of unit design. This led to the creation of the unit editor, which allows players to mix and match various unit parts. Here’s a glimpse of an early sketch of the editor from the design document.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/04d71b396fd56d2355aa372fe8ecd51082291716.jpg[/img]

The availability of a particular weapon or a piece of armor in the editor depends on the sciences researched by the player, as well rare resources found on the game map. In this way, the unit editor isn’t just a self-contained entity, but ties into other game systems, encouraging the player to plan their research ahead and to pay attention to the game map.

Each troop type in the game consists of three main components:

[list]
[*] Infantry: armor, weapon, ammo/shield
[*] Mobile troops: transport platform, weapon, ammunition
[*] Artillery: transport platform, weapon, ammunition
[/list]

Here are a couple of sketches of some of the weapons and transport platforms for Mobile troops.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/1928b09b94efb468529027e093726d391aecbf52.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/7ee4c3019a5748ac2a795714e166ac5b0cad07d8.jpg[/img]

And here’s how our artists have reimagined the sketches of two mountable weapons for a tank from the third epoch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/fd9b958a6f1b6dd15ef80b9e2c4ee372fc764cdd.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/d6a7fc0d1b970e5ab5dd5b3d7b563de3861a432e.jpg[/img]

Respectfully,
Revival: Recolonization Team

notes.title: Revival: Recolonization – plans and ambitions for Open Alpha
notes.content:
Hello to all of Revival’s fans out there! This is the game’s producer, Vasiliy Tedeev.

Before we dive into the new mechanics and changes coming to Revival, I’d like to thank each and every one of you that participated in the Closed Alpha. Your feedback and suggestions were immensely helpful in our attempt to determine what worked well and what didn’t.

Quite a number of the game systems you’ve experienced during the Closed Alpha were either in their infancy or not fully present in the game build. This is something that we plan to address in the coming months, before the game hits Open Alpha.

Here’s what our current roadmap looks like:

[list]
[*] Combat improvements
[*] Edicts 2.0
[*] Diplomacy system
[*] Tribe assimilation update
[*] UX/UI improvements
[/list]

[b]Making combat swift and fun[/b]

To start things off, our team plans to spend the next two iterations on refining combat. Our goal is to ensure combat scenarios provide a more tactical and worthwhile experience by allowing edicts to play a bigger role in battle, without overshadowing the importance of smart unit positioning and outfitting your troops with the right equipment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/b97d73f72beefeabd6011909c44454de75bb9fe1.jpg[/img]

The specific goals for the updated combat system are as follows:

1. Address monotony and reduce the number of easily solvable scenarios – over time, players start seeing the same units and tactics in combat over and over again, which greatly decreases their willingness to engage in such scenarios. Our solution is to provide more opportunities and incentives to try out new tactics with edicts that affect the terrain and various objects on the combat overlay. Think Divinity Original Sin’s interplay between the different elements in combat and you’ll get an idea of what Alex Yegorenkov, the game designer responsible for combat, is going for.

2. Make it swift. Some of the feedback received about combat during the Closed Alpha specifically mentioned the fact that fights are too prolonged, which mirrors our own concerns. So the goal is to make combat as fast as possible, without robbing it of depth.

3. Encourage human input and player creativity. Our team wants to provide more incentives to experiment with the unit editor. Different weapon and armor combinations will (hopefully) provide a more meaningful difference in gameplay rather than just increase attack and defense values.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39245204/cce4f530680bb16000821505b693190c8bb1d180.jpg[/img]

[b]Discord server soon to launch[/b]

Jane and Alexander, who are part of the community management team at HeroCraft PC, are getting ready to launch a discord server for the game fairly soon. This is something that has been requested on several occasions, but we didn’t want to just open a server and forget about it. Instead, Jane and Alexander have prepared something exciting to celebrate the upcoming launch. As much as I want to tell you all about it, now is not the time to spoil the surprise ;)

That’s all for now. Expect one last update to the Closed Alpha build next week, before the team fully focuses on what’s next for Revival: Recolonization.

Stay safe and have fun!
